BEGIN MASTER BRIEF

I want you to build the iOS version of Appraisal Online, a mobile app that provides AI-powered property valuations to consumers and lead-generation services to real estate brokers, lenders, and agents. This is a real product launching in the US and the Philippines. Build it production-ready, not as a demo.
You are Claude Code. You will build both the frontend (React Native with Expo) and the backend (Supabase) in this same project. You are responsible for the entire stack.
Product Overview
Appraisal Online has two sides:
Consumer side (free):

Anyone can enter a property address and details to receive a free AI-generated valuation report in under 60 seconds. The report is delivered as a PDF and an in-app view. Each consumer can request up to 3 free reports per calendar month. After delivery, consumers are asked one question: would they like a local property professional to contact them.
Broker side (paid):

Real estate brokers, lenders, and agents pay an annual membership or a one-time lifetime fee to receive property leads in their cities. There are three membership tiers. Brokers receive leads through the channels they prefer.

Critical Business Rules (Must Be Implemented Exactly)
Free report allowance.
Each consumer account receives 3 free reports per calendar month, resetting on the first. After 3 reports, show a soft paywall directing them to a future premium tier waitlist.
Tier-specific money-back guarantee.
Lifetime: 14 days from payment. After 14 days, NO refunds.
Premium Annual: 30 days from payment. After 30 days, NO refunds until the next renewal date.
Basic Annual: 30 days from payment. After 30 days, NO refunds until the next renewal date.
The refund request flow inside the app must check the broker's tier and the days since payment. If outside the window, block the request with a clear explanation.
Per-city Founder cap.

When a broker selects Lifetime, the system checks each of their selected cities. If any city has already reached 30 Lifetime founders, that city cannot be added. The cap counter must be visible during signup and on a public-facing /founders page that updates in real-time.
Supply-driven marketing allocation.

Once a month, calculate marketing budget allocation per city using a weighted formula: Lifetime members × 3, Premium members × 2, Basic members × 1. Each city's allocation percentage is published on an internal founder dashboard.
Speed gate for leads.
When a consumer report is generated and the consumer opts in to broker contact, the system:
Immediately notifies all Lifetime and Premium brokers in that city via their preferred channels
Adds the lead to the basic-tier weekly digest queue for that city
The basic digest fires every Monday at 9 AM local time, covering the previous Monday-to-Sunday window
Empty digest safeguard.
If a city has fewer than 3 reports in a given week, supplement the digest with curated regional market intelligence so basic members never receive an empty digest.
AI estimate disclaimer.

Every consumer report (in-app view, email body, and PDF) must clearly state: "This is a computer estimate. It is not a licensed appraisal. Banks, courts, and government agencies do not accept this as a formal valuation."
Privacy and opt-in.

No pre-checked consent boxes. Broker contact requires explicit consumer opt-in. Phone number capture is optional and only requested after the consumer agrees to broker contact. Email preferences must be granular and revocable.
Marketing pitch in the app.
Lifetime and Premium tier signup screens must include the supply-driven marketing commitment: "We direct our marketing budget to your cities for the life of your membership."
Refund rate as a health metric.
Track refund rate split by tier (Lifetime vs Annual). If the rolling 30-day rate exceeds 10 percent for any tier, surface this in the founder dashboard as an alert.

Things to Avoid
Do not use Google Apps Script or Google Sheets as the backend. The current pipeline runs on these; you are replacing them with Supabase.
Do not bundle broker contact consent with terms of service acceptance. It must be a separate, explicit opt-in.
Do not pre-check any consent checkboxes.
Do not market lead volume or guarantee specific numbers of leads. The platform guarantees timing of access and city coverage, not lead quantity.

Do not use Apple's in-app purchase for the broker subscription. Use Stripe directly. Apple's IAP is for consumer apps; B2B subscriptions for property professionals are allowed to use external payment.
Do not skip the AI disclaimer anywhere. It must appear in three places per report.
Do not allow Lifetime tier purchases in cities that have reached the 30-founder cap.
Do not show empty weekly digests. The safeguard must always trigger.
Do not market the Lifetime tier as if it is the same as Premium Annual. Use the "founder pass to Premium" framing.
Do not include a 5-year sunset clause or pro-rata refund for Lifetime. This was removed in v05. Lifetime is protected by the 14-day money-back guarantee only.
Do not offer legal advice or legal consultation services to users. The platform is not a legal advisory service. Brokers and consumers are responsible for their own legal compliance.
Do not substitute the AI provider. Use Gemini 2.5 Flash. The existing Apps Script pipeline already uses Gemini.

Notes for Dr. Wallace (Not For Claude Code)
This master brief is designed to be a self-contained project README for Claude Code. Use it as the primary document Claude Code reads at the start of each session.
Why Claude Code for Both Frontend and Backend

Claude Code is well-suited for full-stack work because it has direct file system access, can run shell commands, and can use Bash for testing and deployment. A single agent across frontend and backend reduces handoff overhead and produces more coherent code.

The trade-off: Claude Code is more technical than visual builders like Lovable. You will see more code and need to make more technical decisions. The benefit is full control over the stack and no platform lock-in.
Why Gemini for AI Valuation
Three reasons:
Continuity with the existing Google Apps Script pipeline (which already uses Gemini 2.5 Flash)
Predictable pricing: Gemini 2.5 Flash is approximately $0.075 per 1M input tokens and $0.30 per 1M output tokens, which puts most valuations under $0.03
Latency: Gemini 2.5 Flash is among the fastest production-grade models for structured output
Cost Estimate (MVP Phase, First 6 Months)
Supabase: free tier for first 6 months ($0)
Stripe: 2.9 percent + $0.30 per transaction (variable)
Gemini API: $0.02 to $0.04 per valuation, assume $200 to $400 for first 6 months
Postmark: $15 per month for transactional email
SendGrid: free tier covers most MVP usage
Twilio SMS: $50 to $100 per month (Lifetime tier only)
Expo Application Services: free tier covers MVP
Apple Developer Program: $99 per year
Claude Code subscription: $20 to $100 per month depending on usage tier
Domain: already owned (appraisalonline.ai)
Total estimated 6-month operating cost: $1,000 to $2,000
Claude Code Time Estimate

A solo founder working with Claude Code should plan for 10 to 14 weeks of dedicated work. Claude Code handles the technical heavy lifting but still requires founder input on product decisions, testing, and quality assurance.
